dedupe_keys.name: boario adaptive regional input output model in python

description: BoARIO is an open-source Python implementation of the Adaptive Regional Input-Output (ARIO) model of Hallegatte (2008, 2013), which simulates how a disaster's direct damage to production capacity spreads through inter-industry and inter-regional supply relations and how the economy recovers. Its aims are an accessible and interoperable ARIO implementation plus tools to visualise and analyse simulation outputs and to test the effect of model parameters. It is described in a Journal of Open Source Software paper (Juhel, 2024) and documented with a user guide and API reference. The package is released on PyPI (version 0.7.1, 8 September 2026, Python 3.10 or later) under the GPL-3.0 licence. It runs on multi-regional input-output tables, and the documentation links binary installers, the source repository and an issue tracker. Caveats: results depend on the input-output table and on behavioural parameters such as inventories and overproduction, which the user must choose. For simulation it estimates indirect economic losses and recovery paths after floods, storms or industrial accidents across sectors and regions. Related catalogue records include Acclimate, pymrio and EXIOBASE.
